surfaceForm: particularly for institutions with United-States government research contracts
proposedGenericDecision: Frame as a conditional clause keyed to the role 'institution holding research contracts subject to a foreign-government controlled-information regime', rather than naming the United States specifically.
rationale: The relevance of CUI / SP 800-171 is asserted only for US-government-contract holders. This is a jurisdiction-bound applicability condition. NIST 800-171 itself is a legitimate institution-agnostic standard, but the 'United-States government research contracts' qualifier presumes a specific national contracting context that not all adopting institutions share. Generalize to a role-based condition (institutions subject to a foreign controlled-unclassified-information regime) so the entry stays useful without binding to one country.

surfaceForm: European regulatory framework (section title and contents: GDPR, NIS2, Schrems II, EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, EDPB transfer guidelines)
proposedGenericDecision: Keep the EU instruments as a named 'applicable regional regulatory framework' block, but present it as the instantiation of a generic 'regional data-protection / cybersecurity regulatory layer' role so non-EU adopters can substitute their equivalent instruments. The suite anchors on GDPR as a no-threshold design baseline (per project minimal-necessary-set principle), so GDPR/Schrems/EDPB may legitimately be kept; the framing should signal they are the regional instantiation, not a universal given.
rationale: An entire section presumes the adopting institution sits in the EU legal order (GDPR Art. 32/25/35, NIS2, Schrems II CJEU ruling, EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, EDPB). This is implicit jurisdiction binding: a non-EU university would need its own equivalents. Marked 'keep' rather than 'drop' because the suite intentionally uses GDPR as a size-invariant minimal-set anchor; the recommended treatment is a framing note that these are the regional instantiation plus an optional localization variable, not removal.

surfaceForm: for institutions that provide EU-recognised electronic credentials (eIDAS 2 paragraph)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize the applicability clause to 'institutions that issue regionally-recognised electronic identity / trust-service credentials', so the dependency is role-based rather than tied to the EU eIDAS regime.
rationale: eIDAS 2 is an EU-specific instrument; the relevance condition ('institutions that provide EU-recognised electronic credentials') presumes the EU electronic-identity ecosystem. The role (issuer of recognised electronic credentials) is generalizable; the EU binding is the institution-specific part.

surfaceForm: EDUCAUSE ... The principal venue for higher-education IT discussion in North America
proposedGenericDecision: Keep EDUCAUSE as a named sector-consensus source but soften the descriptor; describe it by role ('a major higher-education IT professional community / sector-consensus body') rather than asserting a single regional primacy, so the catalogue does not implicitly center one continent's sector body.
rationale: EDUCAUSE is a legitimate, citable sector body and should be kept. The mild implicit specificity is the regional framing 'in North America', which, paired with the EU section, signals an implicit North-America/EU dual home for the document. Low confidence: this is descriptive accuracy about EDUCAUSE, not institution-binding; only the regional-primacy phrasing is a candidate for softening.
